characters.name: The Narrator
characters.notes: Unreliable first-person killer who insists he is sane; acute hearing drives the plot

characters.name: The Old Man
characters.notes: Harmless housemate whose pale blue filmy vulture eye obsesses the narrator

characters.name: Three Police Officers
characters.notes: Suave investigators sent after a neighbour reports a shriek

characters.name: Neighbour
characters.notes: Off-screen; hears the shriek and lodges the report

locations_mentioned: the floorboards / scantlings under the chamber
timeline: indeterminate past: idea of murder conceived
one full week of nightly midnight visits (eye always closed)
eighth night, just at midnight: entry and murder
post-murder labors until four o'clock still dark
bell sounds four; police knock and search
officers sit and chat; heartbeat returns; confession
withheld_name_or_twist_rules: Do not confirm the old man is dead or the body hidden before beat B12
Do not let police or audience hear the heartbeat as an objective sound before the narrator's final breakdown; treat it as possibly subjective until B17
Do not reveal the confession or the planks being torn up before beat B18
Keep the narrator's name and exact relationship to the old man unspecified throughout; he remains only 'I'
Do not show blood or gore beyond the clinical dismemberment and tub mention; the horror is auditory and psychological

essential_beats.summary: Narrator opens by insisting he is nervous but not mad; disease sharpened his senses, especially hearing of heaven, earth and hell.
essential_beats.source_evidence: He demands the listener observe how calmly he can tell the whole story.

essential_beats.summary: The murder idea haunts him without object or passion; he loved the old man and wanted no gold; the pale blue vulture eye with film makes his blood run cold.
essential_beats.source_evidence: He decides gradually to kill the old man to rid himself of the eye forever.

essential_beats.summary: He boasts of wise caution and foresight; for the whole week before the killing he is never kinder by day.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Madmen know nothing, yet he proceeded with dissimulation.

essential_beats.summary: Every night at midnight he gently opens the door, thrusts in a closed dark lantern, then his head, taking an hour so as not to wake the sleeper.
essential_beats.source_evidence: He undoes the lantern so a single thin ray falls on the eye; for seven nights the eye is closed so he cannot do the work.

essential_beats.summary: Each morning he boldly enters, speaks heartily, and inquires how the old man passed the night, so the old man never suspects the midnight visits.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Only a profound old man would have guessed.

essential_beats.summary: On the eighth night he is more than usually cautious; a watch's minute hand moves faster than his hand on the door; he feels triumph and chuckles.
essential_beats.source_evidence: The old man stirs as if startled; the room is pitch black with shutters fastened.

essential_beats.summary: His thumb slips on the tin fastening; the old man springs up crying 'Who's there?'
essential_beats.source_evidence: Narrator keeps perfectly still and silent.

essential_beats.summary: For a whole hour he does not move a muscle; the old man remains sitting up in bed listening, just as the narrator has listened to death-watches in the wall.
essential_beats.source_evidence: He never hears the old man lie down again.

essential_beats.summary: A slight groan of mortal terror rises; narrator recognizes it as the sound from a soul overcharged with awe, a sound he himself has made at midnight.
essential_beats.source_evidence: He pities the old man yet chuckles at heart; Death's black shadow has enveloped the victim.

essential_beats.summary: After long patient waiting he opens a tiny crevice in the lantern; a single dim ray like a spider thread falls full upon the open vulture eye.
essential_beats.source_evidence: The eye is wide open; he sees only the dull blue veiled eye and nothing else of the face.

essential_beats.summary: A low dull quick sound like a watch enveloped in cotton reaches his ears; he knows it is the old man's heart; it increases his fury.
essential_beats.source_evidence: He still refrains, scarcely breathes, holds the ray steady while the hellish tattoo grows quicker and louder.

essential_beats.summary: Terror that a neighbour will hear the sound seizes him; with a loud yell he throws open the lantern, leaps into the room, drags the old man down and pulls the heavy bed over him.
essential_beats.source_evidence: The old man shrieks once only; the muffled heart beats many minutes then ceases; narrator confirms stone death and that the eye will trouble him no more.

essential_beats.summary: He works hastily but silently through the waning night: dismembers the corpse, cutting off head, arms and legs.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Wise precautions for concealment of the body.

essential_beats.summary: He lifts three planks, deposits the parts between the scantlings, replaces the boards so cunningly no eye could detect wrong; a tub caught all blood, no stain left.
essential_beats.source_evidence: It is four o'clock, still dark as midnight, when the bell sounds and a knocking comes at the street door.

essential_beats.summary: Three police officers enter with perfect suavity; a neighbour heard a shriek, suspicion of foul play, they are to search the premises.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Narrator smiles, light heart, nothing to fear; claims the shriek was his own in a dream and the old man is absent in the country.

essential_beats.summary: He welcomes them, leads them all over the house, shows the old man's treasures undisturbed, brings chairs into the chamber and sits his own seat directly above the corpse.
essential_beats.source_evidence: In wild audacity of perfect triumph; officers are satisfied by his manner and sit chatting of familiar things.

essential_beats.summary: He grows pale, head aches, a ringing in his ears becomes distinct and is not within his ears; it is the low dull quick sound of the heart again; officers chat on and smile.
essential_beats.source_evidence: He talks more freely then more vehemently, paces, foams, raves, swears, grates the chair on the boards, yet the noise grows louder over all; he believes they hear and mock him.

essential_beats.summary: Unable to bear the hypocritical smiles and the agony, he shrieks that they must dissemble no more, admits the deed, and tells them to tear up the planks: it is the beating of the hideous heart.
